Woolworths Group was founded in 1924 and is headquartered in Sydney (Australia). Beginning as a single store, currently, Woolworths Group is a prominent Australian retail conglomerate with a diverse portfolio of businesses, primarily operating within the retail and consumer sectors (Yahoo Finance 2023). Supermarkets chain is the main operation of Woolworths bringing the most revenue for the company (Yahoo Finance 2023). It operates a vast network of supermarkets across Australia and New Zealand, offering groceries, fresh produce, household items, and a variety of other consumer goods. In New Zealand, the comapny manages the group’s operations through the Countdown supermarket chain (Yahoo Finance 2023). Besides, Woolworths also owns Big W, the group’s discount department store chain, providing a wide range of products including clothing, electronics, toys, and homeware (Yahoo Finance 2023). Moreover, it operates Woolworths Food Group which oversees supply chain and distribution operations for the supermarket and food-related businesses (Yahoo Finance 2023). Woolworths Group, like many companies in Australia, adopts a fiscal year that starts on July 1st and ends on June 30th of the following year. Throughout the fiscal year, Woolworths Group keeps detailed financial records of its operations, revenues, expenses, and investments. These records are maintained in accordance with Australian Accounting Standards.

2. Assess the profitability and efficiency of Woolworths 2.1. The profitability

Analyzing the profitability of a company is crucial in assessing its financial health and performance. In this paper, the profitability of Woolworths is evaluated in the most recent 3 years and based on key metrics, including Gross Margin, EBITDA Margin, Operating Margin, Net Margin, Return on Assets (ROA), and Return on Equity (ROE), while considering industry averages as benchmarks.

Gross margin measures the profitability of a company’s core operations (Schweser 2023). In 2021, the company had a gross margin of 29.30%, which was above the industry median of 28.70%. This indicates healthy profitability from its core business. However, in 2022 and 2023, the gross margin declined to 26.20% and 26.71%, respectively. This may be a cause for concern as it suggests that the company’s ability to maintain profitability in its core operations may be weakening.

Besides, EBITDA margin is a measure of operational profitability before accounting for interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (Schweser 2023). In 2021, the company had a robust EBITDA margin of 9.60%, significantly exceeding the industry median of 5.20%. Moreover, this ratio remained healthy in 2022 and 2023, at 7.70% and 8.60%, respectively. Thus, it demonstrates the company’s ability to generate substantial profits from its operations.

In terms of operating margin, it assesses profitability after considering operating expenses (Schweser 2023). The company’s operating margin improved from 5.10% in 2021 to 4.40% in 2022 but then increased to 4.70% in 2023. Although the ratio improved in 2022, it remained below the industry median of 2.70%. In 2023, it surpassed the industry median, indicating effective cost management.

About net margin, the ratio reflects profitability after accounting forallexpenses, including interest and taxes (Schweser 2023). Woolworths’s net margin was 2.90% in 2021, higher than the industry median of 1.60%. However, it declined slightly to 2.60% in 2022 and 2.50% in 2023. Therefore, it is seen that the net margin consistently outperformed the industry median, implying efficient cost control and profitability.

ROA measures the company’s ability to generate profits relative to its total assets (Schweser 2023). This ratio had improved from 4.10% in 2021 to 4.30% in 2022 and further to 4.87% in 2023. Besides, these figures consistently surpassed the industry average of 2.80%, showing that the asset utilization and enhanced profitability of Woolworths is effective.

ROE evaluates the company’s ability to generate returns for its shareholders (Schweser 2023). In 2021, the company had an impressive ROE of 31.70%, well above the industry median of 8.70%. In 2022, the ROE soared to 42.30%, indicating significant returns for shareholders. Nevertheless, it dropped to 26.30% in 2023, still above the industry average. From that, it is concluded that the company’s ROE has been exceptional, reflecting strong profitability and efficient use of equity. In general, the company has demonstrated strong profitability across key metrics, consistently outperforming industry averages. While there was a slight dip in gross margin in 2022 and 2023, other profitability metrics remained unchanged. Hence, it demonstrates the effective cost management and strong operational performance. Furthermore, the consistently high ROE suggests that the company efficiently generates returns for its shareholders, making it an attractive investment option.

2.2. The efficiency

To evaluate how well Woolworths utilizes its resources to generate sales, manage accounts receivable and accounts payable, and control inventory, several financial indicators are used such as Asset Turnover, A/R Turnover, Average A/R Days, Inventory Turnover, Average Inventory Days, and Average A/P Days.

First, asset turnover measures how efficiently a company uses its assets to create sales (Schweser 2023). The company’s asset turnover improved significantly from 1.43 in 2021 to 1.68 in 2022 and further to 1.92 in 2023. These figures consistently are higher than the industry median of 1.34, meaning that Woolworths effectively utilized its assets to generate sales.

Second, A/R turnover assesses how quickly the company collects accounts receivable (Schweser 2023). In 2021, the company had a high A/R turnover of 108.40, significantly exceeding the industry median of 35.30. While the A/R turnover decreased in 2022 and 2023 to 91.10 and 68.70, respectively, it is still greater than the industry average. Thus, the company’s ability to collect receivables quickly suggests efficient credit management and customer payment practices. This also reflects through average A/R days. In 2021, the company had an exceptionally low Average A/R Days of 3.40, indicating prompt collection of receivables. Although it increased to 4.00 in 2022 and 0.79 in 2023, these figures remained significantly lower than the industry average of 10.30 days in 2021.

Third, inventory turnover evaluates how quickly the company sells its inventory (Schweser 2023). Woolworths’s inventory turnover grew from 10.40 in 2021 to 13.30 in 2022 and 12.92 in 2023. Because the numbers consistently exceeded the industry median of 9.00, it implies the efficient inventory management and rapid product turnover. The company’s ability to minimize the time inventory sits on its shelves also demonstrated through average inventory days of the company. In 2021, Woolworths had an average inventory days of 35, indicating relatively fast inventory turnover. This figure further improved to 27.30 in 2022 and slightly increased to 28.24 in 2023, remaining below the industry median.

Last but not least, average A/P days measures the average number of days it takes the company to pay its suppliers (Schweser 2023). The company had an average A/P days of 49.40, implying a reasonable payment cycle in 2021. Nevertheless, in 2022, it decreased significantly to 40.90 and raised to 56.65 in 2023. Despite these fluctuations, the figures still within industry averages. Overall, Woolworths has demonstrated strong efficiency across key metrics, consistently better than industry averages in asset utilization, accounts receivable management, inventory turnover, and accounts payable practices. It can be seen that efficient asset utilization and inventory management contribute to higher sales and better cash flow. Besides, the company’s ability to collect receivables quickly and manage inventory efficiently also shows effective working capital management.

3. Non-financial factors affecting investment decision in Woolworths

When contemplating an investment in a company like Woolworths, it’s crucial to consider not only its financial performance but also non-financial information, particularly sustainability factors. These factors can provide valuable insights into the company’s long-term viability and its alignment with environmental, social, and governance (ESG) principles. First, investors should consider about environmental sustainability factor. Understanding the company’s efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and its commitment to sustainability goals is crucial. A company that actively works to reduce its carbon footprint is more likely to adapt well to evolving environmental regulations and consumer preferences (Parikh et al. 2023). Thus, information on how Woolworths manages waste and promotes recycling can be indicative of its commitment to environmental sustainability (Woolworths 2023). Reducing waste and implementing recycling programs demonstrate responsible environmental stewardship. Moreover, investor also needs to assesses the company’s efforts to source products sustainably, such as responsibly sourced seafood and ethically produced goods, because it can reflect a commitment to environmentally friendly practices. From that, it is seen that companies with well-defined sustainability goals and transparent reporting mechanisms aremore likely to be committed to long-term sustainability (Parikh et al. 2023). Second, social responsibility of company is also a vital factor which investors should pay attention. Evaluating the company’s labor practices, including fair wages, workplace safety, and diversity and inclusion initiatives, can help determine its commitment to social responsibility (Parikh et al. 2023). A company that values its employees is likely to foster a positive corporate culture. According to sustainability report 2023 of Woolworths, it involvement in local communities, charitable contributions, and initiatives supporting education and healthcare can highlight its commitment to social well-being (Woolworths 2023). Furthermore, the company’s commitment to product quality, safety, and transparency is also essential, especially in the food retail industry, where consumer trust is paramount. Third, governance structure and ethics are important for investors to assess. A well-structured board with diverse perspectives is often associated with good governance (Parikh et al. 2023). Besides, investigating any history of ethical violations, legal issues, or corporate scandals can help gauge the company’s commitment to ethical conduct and integrity. Finally, in investment decision making, industry comparisons can offer a broader perspective on company’s relative strengths and weaknesses. Therefore, it is seen that non-financial information and sustainability factors are essential because they go beyond short-term financial gains and losses. They provide insights into a company’s resilience, reputation, and ability to create long-term value while addressing societal and environmental challenges. Investors increasingly recognize that companies which prioritize sustainability are more likely to mitigate risks, attract conscientious consumers, and adapt successfully to a rapidly changing business landscape (Andrey 2023). Hence, considering non-financial information and sustainability factors when contemplating an investment in Woolworths or any company is essential.

4. Importance of the auditor’s opinion

The independent auditors for Woolworths in their 2023 annual report were Deloitte. Deloitte is one of the “Big Four” accounting firms globally and is known for its expertise in auditing and assurance services. In their auditor’s opinion provided in the annual report, Deloitte affirmed the following key points. First, Deloitte indicated that the financial report of Woolworths Group gives a true and fair view of the financial position (Woolworths 2023). In other words, in the auditors’ professional judgment, the financial statements accurately represent the financial status of the company as of that date. Second, the auditors also noted that the financial report complies with the Corporations Act 2001, which is a critical regulatory framework governing financial reporting and disclosurerequirements for companies in Australia (Woolworths 2023). This compliance confirms that Woolworths adhered to the legal and accounting standards set forth by Australian law. Third, Deloitte’s opinion stated that the financial report complies with Australian Accounting Standards (Woolworths 2023). These standards provide guidelines and rules for the preparation and presentation of financial statements, ensuring consistency and comparability across companies in Australia. From that, Deloitte, as the independent auditor, provided an unqualified opinion for financial report of Woolworths. It means the auditors found no material misstatements or irregularities in the financial statements. Report of auditors is of paramount importance to shareholders of a company like Woolworths Group Limited. It serves as a critical tool for assessing the reliability and integrity of the company’s financial statements and provides shareholders with assurance regarding the accuracy of the financial information presented in the annual report. A company is audited by a reputable auditing firm can enhances investors’ confidence in the report’s objectivity (Drabek and Merkova 2015). It means that shareholders rely on auditors to provide an unbiased evaluation of the company’s financial health, free from any conflicts of interestas the confirmation that the financial statements, including the balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow statement, have been examined thoroughly (Drabek and Merkova 2015). Shareholders need this assurance to make informed investment decisions.Besides, report of auditors often includes insights intothe company’s internal controls and risk management processes. From that, shareholders can have more chance to know if any significant issues or weaknesses have been identified during the audit, as this can impact the company’s stability and governance. Moreover, the auditor’s report plays a role in fostering investors invest in Woolworths. When shareholders have trust in the accuracy of the financial statements, they are more likely to remain invested in the company and even attract new investors (Drabek and Merkova 2015). Especially, those who actively manage their portfolios, can use the information in the auditor’s report to make decisions about buying, holding, or selling Woolworths’ shares. It is a critical reference point for evaluating the company’s financial health.
